entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Raj Kumar Srivastava,D.M.Tripathi,Rahul Tiwari,Sita Ram Sharma
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.
The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the daughter of the informant was married at around 11 years ago with the applicant.
It was also alleged that the applicant was having extra marital relation with many women.
It was also alleged that on 25.06.2022, the applicant along with his brother and sister-in-law had committed the murder of the daughter of the informant.

3. The Counsel for the applicant draws my attention to the postmortem report which indicates a ligature mark 30cm x 2cm all around the neck and apart from the said, no visible injury since over the body.

In the light of the said mark, the submission of the learned Counsel for the applicant is that the conclusion regarding cause of death in the postmortem as asphyxia due to antemortem Ajeet vs State Of U.P. on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158427745/
1

entities.text: antemortem Ajeet vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: strangulation is inherently incorrect as the cause of death is clearly antemortem hanging.
He argues that based upon the said opinion expressed in the postmortem report, the applicant was taken into custody.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents.
4. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the submissions made at the bar; prima facie, from the mark seen over the body, the suggestion given in the postmortem report that it was on account of antemortem strangulation is prima facie incorrect and the said cannot be conclusively determined at this stage; the applicant is in custody since 27.06.2022 and there are no specific assertion of demand of dowry and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
6.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Ajeet be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.271 of 2022, under Sections 302, 120B, 498A IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Civil Lines, District Meerut on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
